video_title: LIVE: Pelicans vs. Grizzlies Postgame Interviews 11/13/2026

quotes.speaker: Jamahl Mosley
quotes.summary_phrase: Jamahl Mosley on defensive adjustments needed after third consecutive loss
quotes.excerpt: not being happy doesn't solve the problem. So there's probably some adjustments need to be made
quotes.quote: Not being happy. But not being happy doesn't solve the problem. And so there's probably some adjustments need to be made, the way we're guarding or not, lack thereof, and that's part of on the coaching, what we've got to do there, what we've got to do there. But again, there's a will, there's a want, there's a desire, there's rotations, there's not straight line drives, not blowbys. The want to sit down and guard, but then also if you do get beat, got to have help. Those are a lot of situations. Now, they shot the break side of the basketball, some highly contested ones, some wide open ones because they did a great job reading the defense, but we've got to be better there and we will be.
quotes.social_post: Jamahl Mosley admits the Pelicans need to adjust their defensive scheme after a third straight loss. He says the team must stop giving up straight line drives and improve their help rotations to address recent struggles.

structured.context: Head coach Jamahl Mosley discusses the need for defensive adjustments after a loss.

quotes.speaker: Jamahl Mosley
quotes.summary_phrase: Jamahl Mosley on defensive rotations and help defense against downhill attackers
quotes.excerpt: they're putting their head down going, which forces our bigs to come across the lane and help
quotes.quote: Some of it is the pick up point. You know, we talk about crawling into the ball, getting into the ball, heating up, but these guards on these teams are very good at getting downhill and attacking, so they're putting their head down going, which forces our bigs to come across the lane and help. And when they come across the lane, they've got to have a second line defender, a back line to be able to crack down and help them. That's why the some of the dump offs are happening. There'll be some adjustments made to that to where we're going to have to force some things that normally we weren't used to giving up, but we're going to have to say, okay, we'll live with certain things here and not give up as much rim and wide open looks from the three that we've been giving up being in rotation.
quotes.social_post: Jamahl Mosley on the defensive adjustments needed to stop downhill attackers. He says the team will have to force opponents into different looks to avoid giving up easy rim attempts and wide open threes.

structured.context: Jamahl Mosley explains the defensive rotation challenges when facing guards who attack the rim.

quotes.speaker: Jamahl Mosley
quotes.summary_phrase: Jamahl Mosley on fixing defensive issues and maintaining team energy
quotes.excerpt: the energy, the spirit, the hard play, like we were there in moments, got it to three
quotes.quote: No, we can fix this one. Yeah, I mean, the energy, the spirit, the hard play, like we were there in moments, got it to three, and so that's what you like to see. But again, these are the adjustments that as a coach you have to make and know that a certain scheme works certain ways with certain people and it doesn't work with others. So we'll have to be better. We're not going to change the way that we're going to try to crawl into the basketball, be physical, do the best as we can without fouling, without getting into the bonus with the seven minute mark in each quarter. We've got to be smarter there, but the other side of it is just making sure that we're forcing things that we want versus being overly aggressive at the wrong time.
quotes.social_post: Jamahl Mosley says the team needs to be smarter about avoiding fouls early in quarters. He remains committed to the team's aggressive defensive identity while acknowledging the need for better situational awareness.

structured.context: Jamahl Mosley addresses the team's defensive schemes and the need for smarter aggression.

quotes.speaker: Jamahl Mosley
quotes.summary_phrase: Jamahl Mosley on the difficulty of evaluating lineup data due to injuries
quotes.excerpt: it's hard to find the data when you have guys bumping in, bumping out
quotes.quote: You know the interesting part about that question, it's hard to find the data when you have guys bumping in, bumping out, you know, what three man combo works. We haven't had many of those. So it's trying to find the right combinations, but 13, 14 games into the season with guys going down, guys stepping in, guys stepping out, you know, you had a situation, you know, you had Trey Murphy was in the rotation for a while, then he goes down. Eves was early on, then he goes down, then Trey Murphy was in, then he bumps out. These are not excuses, these are the reality of not being able to find the right sample size because you don't have enough games to really measure it.
quotes.social_post: Jamahl Mosley explains why it is difficult to evaluate lineup data right now. With players like Trey Murphy in and out of the rotation due to injuries, he says the team hasn't had the sample size to find the right combinations.

structured.context: Jamahl Mosley explains that frequent injuries make it difficult to evaluate effective lineup combinations.

quotes.speaker: Jamahl Mosley
quotes.summary_phrase: Jamahl Mosley on rebounding and transition defense
quotes.excerpt: if you're not making those shots, you got to crash the glass, give yourself other opportunities
quotes.quote: Part of that is going to be if you're not making those shots, you got to crash the glass, give yourself other opportunities. And I think when we went on that run, we were getting stops and then we were getting out and getting some easy baskets. When the stop when the run stopped, we missed a lot of easy chippy layups as well as wide open threes, and they were able to break out in transition to get that thing pushed back up. So part of it is, you know what, you got to step in and knock your shot down and take it when you're open. The other side of it is can't play in a crowd to turn it over, and if you're going to play in that lane, we got to be able to finish. Those are all pieces, and if we're not getting there, I have a problem and I can we can adjust that.
quotes.social_post: Jamahl Mosley on the team's offensive struggles. He says missing easy layups and turning the ball over in crowds has made it difficult to set the defense in transition.

structured.context: Jamahl Mosley discusses how missed shots and turnovers negatively impact the team's transition defense.

quotes.speaker: Jamahl Mosley
quotes.summary_phrase: Jamahl Mosley on team performance and fan expectations
quotes.excerpt: I'm disappointed by how we've played and that the fans are looking at it like this
quotes.quote: Absolutely. And I said this prior, too. I'm disappointed by how we've played and that the fans are looking at it like this is not what they're expecting. I understand that. I'm not ducking that, I'm not shying away from it. I know what we said we wanted to how we wanted to play, the product we wanted to put on the floor, and you saw it for that a stretch of the early games, then you saw it for the one when we win four in a row. So it's there. And that's what we have to understand, this is a process. We'll keep talking about that in some form or fashion, but just like the NBA there's highs, there's lows. We're going to find that stride because this these guys' energy and spirit was right. Now we just got to put the pieces together and that's on me as a coach to figure out the ways to put these guys in the best position to be successful. But yeah, if I'm the fans, I'm up I'm looking at it like this there needs to be better, and we will be better. That's why there's 82 games in a season.
quotes.social_post: Jamahl Mosley on the team's recent slump. If I am the fans I am looking at it like this there needs to be better and we will be better. He says he is not shying away from the disappointment surrounding the current product on the floor.

structured.context: Jamahl Mosley acknowledges fan frustration with the team's recent performance and emphasizes the long season.

quotes.speaker: Jamahl Mosley
quotes.summary_phrase: Jamahl Mosley on managing injuries and next-man-up mentality
quotes.excerpt: it's never easy, but that is part of the league and this is what a lot of teams
quotes.quote: You know it's never easy, but that is part of the league and this is what a lot of teams are dealing with. There's a lot of teams dealing with a lot of injuries and you just got to find the way. We talk about next man up, next man up mentality offensively, next man up mentality defensively, and that's what we're going to have to continue to do this by committee over and over, whether that's changing a scheme, adjusting some things, but it's going to stay focused on being making sure we're pressuring the basketball the right way. But now we've got to start forcing teams to do what we want them to do versus them keeping us in rotation and moving in different spots. And then we've got to when we do rotate, we've got to understand who we're closing out to, how we're closing out, not allowing straight line drives, and if a guy gets gets beat, we have to know his help is there.
quotes.social_post: Jamahl Mosley on managing the injury bug. He says the team must continue to rely on a next man up mentality by committee while adjusting schemes to keep the pressure on the basketball.

structured.context: Jamahl Mosley discusses the team's next-man-up mentality while dealing with ongoing injury issues.

quotes.speaker: Jamahl Mosley
quotes.summary_phrase: Jamahl Mosley on preventing offensive mistakes from impacting defense
quotes.excerpt: when you're open, knock it down and take it when you're open. The other side of it is
quotes.quote: It sounds like a simple answer, but really it is is when you're open, knock it down and take it when you're open. The other side of it is can't play in a crowd to turn it over, and if you're going to play in that lane, you got to be able to finish. And if you don't finish, then you got to spray out for those knockdown feet set threes, which we got quite a few of them. So those are the pieces that allow your offense to just be have balance to so you're able to balance the floor getting back on defense. So the right shot at the right time, the right play, the right pass, that the game will tell you what that looks like. And then you've got to make a conscious effort to sprint back after the ball's either going in or you know, or it doesn't, because these guys were pushing it on make or miss.
quotes.social_post: Jamahl Mosley emphasizes the importance of shot selection and transition defense. He says the team must make a conscious effort to sprint back on defense regardless of whether their shots go in or not.

structured.context: Jamahl Mosley explains the importance of shot selection and floor balance to prevent opponent transition opportunities.
